card.name: Malhao
card.tagline: Lively Portuguese folk couples dance from the Minho.
card.profile: Malhao is a lively Portuguese folk dance and song from northwestern Portugal, especially the Minho region, danced by couples in lines or circular formation with quick rhythmic footwork, accompanied by guitarra portuguesa and tambourine. Its name likely derives from an agricultural implement; the song tells of the 'malhao' (winnower), reflecting rural harvest-celebration origins. Performed at festivals such as Festa das Cruzes in Barcelos (Portugal.com; Society of Folk Dance Historians).
card.insight: Malhao has many local variants ('Malhao de Cinfaes,' 'Malhao de Agueda') recorded by fado singer Amalia Rodrigues; per folk-dance historians it has changed little in over a century.
